answer:
Use the solver twoPhaseEulerFoam in steady-state mode.
The pipe is horizontal, with an inner diameter of 0.05 m and a length of 1 m, aligned along the x-axis.
Generate a single-block cylindrical mesh with approximately 200 cells in the axial direction, 40 cells in the radial direction, and 36 cells in the circumferential direction.
Set the water phase properties to rho = 1000 kg/m³ and nu = 1e-6 m²/s.
Set the oil phase properties to rho = 850 kg/m³ and nu = 1e-4 m²/s.
In 0/U, set the inlet patch as type fixedValue with value uniform (1 0 0).
In 0/U, set the outlet patch as type inletOutletVelocity with value uniform (1 0 0).
In 0/U, set the wall patch as type noSlip.
In 0/p, set the inlet patch as type zeroGradient.
In 0/p, set the outlet patch as type fixedValue with value uniform 0.
In 0/p, set the wall patch as type neumann with value 0.
In 0/alpha.water, set the inlet patch as type fixedValue with value uniform 0.3.
In 0/alpha.water, set the outlet patch as type zeroGradient.
In 0/alpha.water, set the wall patch as type zeroGradient.
In system/fvSolution, set the steady-state residual control for U, p, and alpha.water to 1e-6.
In system/fvSchemes, use upwind for div schemes on U and alpha.water, and linear for grad schemes.
The gravity vector is set to (0 0 0) since the pipe is horizontal and gravity effects on the two-phase distribution are to be neglected in this base case.
The runtime controls (controlDict) are set to write and adjust every 1000 iterations with a maximum of 100000 iterations.
